issues.description: cad fea exits 4 / reports BELOW TARGET for 'payload' (plain SF 1.25) even though the away-from-supports SF is 3.6; the peak sits on the horn screw-hole walls (idealised clamp). The task says to judge by the away-from-supports number, but the headline verdict and exit code still use the plain one, so a passing design looks failing.

A tapered beam joined to hub/tip cylinders by a polygon leaves nearly tangent concave kinks; fillet of these failed with a generic FILLET_FAILED (even for radius 6 with hint 'below ~4.5 mm'). I built the beam with exact tangent points to avoid inside corners instead.

A rectangular beam unioned with hub/tip circles of equal width gives near-tangent concave vertical edges and a tangent junction at the tip; fillet of those failed with FILLET_FAILED even at 3 mm. I switched to a tangent-line hull outline (computed by hand) which has no concave corners at all.

'cad build' exits 4 (validation failed) when the plain safety factor is below target, even though the task says to judge by the away-from-supports value. Final design: pushrod plain SF 3.2, payload plain SF 1.85 (at the clamped screw-hole edge) but away-from-supports SF 4.8.

Filleting all concave edges at radius 3 with a beam wider than the 14 mm tip failed (FILLET_FAILED). The failing edges were listed by coordinates but the cause was not explained, and the 'try a radius below ~1 mm' hint was misleading. After the failed build, `cad fea` silently analysed the previous revision.

Pass/fail semantics: at --quality fine the plain payload safety factor at the fixed horn holes is 1.6 while the away-from-supports value is ~3. The CLI exits 4 (VALIDATION_FAILED) on the plain value even though the task rule says to judge away from supports. Results also shift 5-10% between draft/normal/fine near the margin.
No tapered / variable-width beam helper; a mass-efficient design (wide at the hub, narrow at the tip) needs profile or loft work.

suggestions.suggestion: Let Study take an option (or report a second verdict line) so 'ok' is judged on away_from_supports_and_sharp_edges when the peak is flagged PEAK_AT_SUPPORT.
Provide a Profile helper for the tangent hull of two circles (slot with different end diameters / 'tapered slot').
Report mass in cad fea / sweep output alongside SF (sweep does, fea does not).
A Profile helper for the tangent hull of two circles (slot/taper) would avoid hand-computed tangent points.
Report a per-study pass/fail that uses the away-from-supports value explicitly so build validation matches the stated criterion.
cad inspect could list concave (sharp inside) edges so the no-sharp-corner requirement can be verified directly.
Let `cad fea` use the away-from-supports safety factor for ok/exit code when PEAK_AT_SUPPORT applies, or offer a flag for it.
When a build fails, make `cad fea` refuse to run or state loudly which revision it analyses.
Let `cad sweep` sweep two parameters (or fillet radius) and report the lightest passing combination under a mass limit.
Explain FILLET_FAILED causes using the geometry (e.g. edge ends on a tangent or short edge).
